fullPassage:
Dr. Hahn Heung-soo grew up in Korea after the Korean War. Having experienced hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people who were starving. After completing his studies in agriculture, he was offered a position at Cambridge University. However, he chose to go to Nigeria instead, a country that had been destroyed by a civil war. Over two million people had died, and more than 500,000 were starving.

Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was defenseless against diseases and had a very low yield. It was not considered a cash crop, so no one had invested in improving it. Dr. Hahn knew that if he could develop better varieties of cassava, he could rescue millions from hunger. He flew to Brazil to collect original cassava seeds, and then crossed them with a disease-resistant plant. It took him five years to develop new varieties that were both high-yielding and resistant to diseases.

Distributing the new cassava was just as challenging as developing it. Nigerian farmers would not listen to a foreigner telling them how to cultivate their land. So Dr. Hahn gave out the new cassava for free at local markets, churches, and schools. He even planted the new varieties secretly in farmers’ fields. When the farmers saw the superiority of the new cassava, they began to adopt it willingly.

Thanks to Dr. Hahn’s efforts, Nigeria became the world’s largest cassava producer. In 1983, the Yoruba tribe honored him as a chief, giving him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers.” He also developed improved varieties of yam, sweet potato, and banana. After spending 23 years in Nigeria, he left in 1994.

Dr. Hahn once said, “If you have faith that what you do will benefit humanity, I believe that you must sacrifice yourself.” His contributions to agriculture earned him numerous awards, including the UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize, which honors outstanding contributions to the fight against illiteracy.

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn Heung-soo grew up in Korea after the Korean War. __________ hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people who were starving. After completing his studies in agriculture, he was offered a position at Cambridge University.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(decided)보다 앞선 경험을 나타내는 완료 분사구문 Having experienced가 적절하다. "굶주림을 직접 경험했기 때문에"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ Having experienced: 완료 분사구문 → 주절보다 먼저 일어난 동작
❌ ① Experience: 동사원형 단독 사용 불가
❌ ② Experienced: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ④ To experience: to부정사 → 목적 의미로 문맥 부적절
det.tip: 완료 분사구문 Having + p.p.: 주절보다 먼저 일어난 동작/원인을 나타냄

questions.passage: Having experienced hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people __________ were starving. After completing his studies in agriculture, he was offered a position at Cambridge University.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 people(사람)을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 who가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② who: 사람 선행사(people) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① which: 사물 선행사용 → people은 사람
❌ ③ what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사(people)가 있으므로 불가
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사람) + who + 동사: 사람을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was defenseless against diseases and had a very low yield. It was not considered a cash crop, __________ no one had invested in improving it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "환금작물로 여겨지지 않았기 때문에 아무도 개량에 투자하지 않았다"는 인과 접속 → so가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① so: 결과를 나타내는 등위접속사 → "그래서 아무도 투자하지 않았다"
❌ ② such: such + 명사 구조 → 문법적으로 부적절
❌ ③ very: 부사 → 접속 기능 없음
❌ ④ too: 부사 → 접속 기능 없음
det.tip: so(접속사): 앞 절의 결과를 이어줌. "A, so B" = A이므로 B이다

questions.passage: Thanks to Dr. Hahn’s efforts, Nigeria became the world’s largest cassava producer. In 1983, the Yoruba tribe honored him as a chief, __________ him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(honored)의 동시 동작/부연을 나타내는 분사구문 giving이 적절하다. "추장으로 추대하면서 칭호를 주었다"
det.analysis:
✅ ② giving: 동시동작 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① gave: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ③ to give: to부정사 → 문맥상 동시동작이 자연스러움
❌ ④ having given: 완료분사 → 주절보다 앞선 동작 아님
❌ ⑤ given: 과거분사 → 수동의 의미로 부적절
det.tip: 동시동작 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작을 부연

questions.passage: Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was ①<u>defenseless</u> against diseases and had a very low ②<u>yield</u>. It was not ③<u>considering</u> a cash crop, so no one had ④<u>invested</u> in improving it. Dr. Hahn ⑤<u>knew</u> that if he could develop better varieties of cassava, he could rescue millions from hunger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ considering → considered: 카사바가 환금작물로 "여겨지는" 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 considered가 적절하다. "It was not considered a cash crop" = 환금작물로 여겨지지 않았다
det.analysis:
❌ ③ considering(능동) → considered(수동): 카사바가 스스로 여기는 것이 아니라 여겨지는 것
✅ ① defenseless: 형용사 → "방어력이 없는" 올바름
✅ ② yield: 명사 → "수확량" 올바름
✅ ④ invested: 과거분사 → "투자했다" 올바름
✅ ⑤ knew: 과거형 → "알았다" 올바름
det.tip: 능동/수동: 주어가 동작의 대상이면 be + p.p.(수동). consider → be considered(~로 여겨지다)

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn Heung-soo grew up in Korea after the Korean War. Having experienced hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people who were starving. After completing his studies in agriculture, he was offered a position at Cambridge University. However, he chose to go to Nigeria instead, a country that had been destroyed by a civil war. Over two million people had died, and more than 500,000 were starving.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "he was offered a position at Cambridge University. However, he chose to go to Nigeria instead" → 케임브리지 대신 나이지리아를 선택했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 케임브리지 대신 나이지리아 선택: 본문과 일치
❌ ① 케임브리지에서 연구 시작: 거절하고 나이지리아로 감
❌ ③ 50만 명 사망: 200만 명 사망, 50만 명은 굶주림
❌ ④ 나이지리아 출생: 한국에서 성장
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 핵심 숫자와 사실을 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: 한 박사는 케임브리지 대학에서 연구를 시작했다.
한 박사는 케임브리지 대학 대신 나이지리아를 선택했다.

questions.passage: Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was defenseless against diseases and had a very low yield. It was not considered a cash crop, so no one had invested in improving it. Dr. Hahn knew that if he could develop better varieties of cassava, he could rescue millions from hunger. He flew to Brazil to collect original cassava seeds, and then crossed them with a disease-resistant plant. It took him five years to develop new varieties that were both high-yielding and resistant to diseases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "It took him five years to develop new varieties" → 5년이 걸렸다. "3년"은 본문과 다르다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 3년: 본문은 "five years"(5년)
✅ ① 주식: "staple food of Nigeria" → 일치
✅ ② 브라질: "flew to Brazil to collect original cassava seeds" → 일치
✅ ④ 질병 저항+고수확: "high-yielding and resistant to diseases" → 일치
det.tip: 숫자 관련 선택지는 본문의 정확한 수치와 반드시 대조

ch: 한 박사는 브라질에서 원래 카사바 종자를 수집했다.
새 품종은 질병에 강하고 수확량이 높았다.

questions.passage: Thanks to Dr. Hahn’s efforts, Nigeria became the world’s largest cassava producer. In 1983, the Yoruba tribe honored him as a chief, giving him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers.” He also developed improved varieties of yam, sweet potato, and banana. After spending 23 years in Nigeria, he left in 1994.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한국전쟁 후 굶주림을 경험한 한 박사가 나이지리아에서 카사바를 개량하여 기아를 해결하고 추장으로 추대된 이야기 → 한 박사의 헌신적 농업 연구와 나이지리아 기여
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 한 박사의 헌신과 기여: 글 전체의 핵심 주제
❌ ① 내전 원인: 배경일 뿐 주제 아님
❌ ② 영양학적 가치: 언급되지 않음
❌ ④ 브라질 농업사: 종자 수집 장소일 뿐
❌ ⑤ 요루바족 문화: 추대 사건의 배경일 뿐
det.tip: 글의 주제: 인물 중심 글에서 핵심 업적과 그 의의가 주제

ch: 한 박사의 헌신적인 농업 연구와 나이지리아 기여

questions.passage: Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was defenseless against diseases and had a very low yield. It was not considered a cash crop, so no one had invested in improving it. Dr. Hahn knew that if he could develop better varieties of cassava, he could __________ millions from hunger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 카사바를 개량하면 수백만 명을 기아에서 구할(rescue) 수 있다는 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ② rescue: 기아(hunger)로부터 구하다 → 문맥 일치
❌ ① export: 수출하다 → 사람을 수출할 수 없음
❌ ③ compete with: ~와 경쟁하다 → 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ educate: 교육하다 → 기아 해결과 직접 연결 안 됨
det.tip: rescue + 사람 + from + 위험: ~로부터 구하다

questions.passage: So Dr. Hahn gave out the new cassava for free at local markets, churches, and schools. He even planted the new varieties secretly in farmers’ fields. When the farmers saw the __________ of the new cassava, they began to adopt it willingly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 농부들이 새 카사바의 우수성(superiority)을 보고 자발적으로 채택하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ superiority: 우수성/우월함 → 기존보다 뛰어난 것을 보고 채택
❌ ① danger: 위험 → 채택 동기로 부적절
❌ ② inferiority: 열등함 → 반의어
❌ ④ uniformity: 균일성 → 문맥과 무관
det.tip: superiority(우수성) ↔ inferiority(열등함): 새 품종의 장점을 확인 → 채택

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn once said, “If you have faith that what you do will benefit humanity, I believe that you must __________ yourself.” His contributions to agriculture earned him numerous awards.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인류에 도움이 된다는 믿음이 있다면 자신을 희생해야(sacrifice) 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① sacrifice: 희생하다 → 23년간 나이지리아 헌신과 일치
❌ ② promote: 홍보/승진시키다 → 자신을 홍보하는 것은 문맥과 불일치
❌ ③ enrich: 풍요롭게 하다 → 문맥과 불일치
❌ ④ protect: 보호하다 → 자신을 보호하는 것은 희생과 반대
det.tip: sacrifice oneself = 자신을 희생하다. 한 박사의 헌신적 삶이 핵심 단서

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn Heung-soo grew up in Korea after the Korean War. Having experienced hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people who were __________  (starve). After completing his studies in agriculture, he was offered a position at Cambridge University.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: starve(동사) → starving(현재분사/형용사): "were + ~ing" 진행형 또는 "굶주리고 있는"이라는 의미의 현재분사
det.analysis:
starve(동사) → starving(현재분사)
were ____: 과거진행형(were starving) = 굶주리고 있었다
det.tip: be동사 + ~ing = 진행형: were starving = 굶주리고 있었다

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn flew to Brazil to collect original cassava seeds, and then crossed them with a disease-__________ (resist) plant. It took him five years to develop new varieties that were both high-yielding and resistant to diseases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: resist(동사) → resistant(형용사): 복합형용사 disease-resistant(질병에 강한). 명사 plant를 수식.
det.analysis:
resist(동사) → resistant(형용사)
disease-resistant plant = 질병에 저항력이 있는 식물
det.tip: resist → resistant / differ → different / import → important — 동사/명사 → -ant 형용사 변환

questions.passage: Thanks to Dr. Hahn’s efforts, Nigeria became the world’s largest cassava producer. In 1983, the Yoruba tribe honored him as a chief, giving him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers.”
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 요루바족이 한 박사에게 부여한 칭호를 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "giving him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers”" → 세리키 아그베
det.analysis:
요루바족이 부여한 칭호 = Seriki Agbe
의미: King of Farmers(농부의 왕)
det.tip: 고유명사/칭호는 대문자로 시작: Seriki Agbe

questions.passage: Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria, but it was defenseless against diseases and had a very low yield. It was not considered a cash crop, so no one had invested in improving it.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 나이지리아의 주식(staple food)으로 언급된 작물을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "Cassava was the staple food of Nigeria" → 카사바
det.analysis:
나이지리아의 주식 = Cassava
staple food = 주식, 주요 식량
det.tip: staple food = 주식/주요 식량: 한 나라나 지역의 기본 식량

questions.passage: Thanks to Dr. Hahn’s efforts, Nigeria became the world’s largest cassava producer. In 1983, the Yoruba tribe honored him as a chief, giving him the title “Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers.” He also developed improved varieties of yam, sweet potato, and banana. After spending 23 years in Nigeria, he left in 1994.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 "Seriki Agbe"의 뜻을 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "“Seriki Agbe,” which means “King of Farmers”" → 농부의 왕
det.analysis:
Seriki Agbe의 의미 = King of Farmers
which means = ~를 의미하는
det.tip: which means "~" = ~를 의미하다 → 인용부호 안의 내용이 정답

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn Heung-soo grew up in Korea after the Korean War. Having experienced hunger firsthand, he decided to devote his life to helping people who were starving.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Dr. Hahn experienced hunger firsthand after the Korean War."

det.korean: "grew up in Korea after the Korean War. Having experienced hunger firsthand" → 한국전쟁 후 굶주림을 직접 경험 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "experienced hunger firsthand" = 직접 굶주림을 경험 → 진술과 일치
det.tip: firsthand = 직접, 몸소: 간접이 아닌 본인이 직접 경험

questions.passage: Distributing the new cassava was just as challenging as developing it. Nigerian farmers would not listen to a foreigner telling them how to cultivate their land. So Dr. Hahn gave out the new cassava for free at local markets, churches, and schools.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Nigerian farmers eagerly accepted the new cassava from the beginning."

det.korean: 본문: "Nigerian farmers would not listen to a foreigner" → 농부들은 처음에 외국인의 말을 듣지 않았다. "처음부터 열심히 받아들였다"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "would not listen" → 거부 ≠ "eagerly accepted"(열심히 수용)
det.tip: "would not listen" = 들으려 하지 않았다 — 처음에는 거부, 나중에 수용

questions.passage: He also developed improved varieties of yam, sweet potato, and banana. After spending 23 years in Nigeria, he left in 1994.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Dr. Hahn spent 23 years in Nigeria before leaving in 1994."

det.korean: "After spending 23 years in Nigeria, he left in 1994" → 23년 후 1994년에 떠남 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "spending 23 years" + "left in 1994" → 진술과 정확히 일치
det.tip: 숫자와 연도를 정확히 대조: 23년, 1994년

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn once said, “If you have faith that what you do will benefit humanity, I believe that you must sacrifice yourself.” His contributions to agriculture earned him numerous awards, including the UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize, which honors outstanding contributions to the fight against illiteracy.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize honors contributions to agricultural research."

det.korean: 본문: "which honors outstanding contributions to the fight against illiteracy(문맹 퇴치)" → 농업 연구가 아닌 문맹 퇴치에 대한 공로를 기리는 상이다. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize = 문맹 퇴치 공헌 ≠ 농업 연구(agricultural research)
det.tip: 상의 목적을 정확히 파악: Literacy Prize = 문맹 퇴치(illiteracy) 관련
